interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. Favorable findings include a negative surgical margin (0.0), absence of seminal vesicle invasion (0.0), absence of lymphovascular invasion (0.0), and negative findings for extraprostatic extension (0.0). The surgical pathology showed a Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2) and a pT2 stage. Countervailing factors include the preoperative PSA of 11 and the absence of lymph node removal, resulting in an uncharacterized nodal status (pNx, as no nodes were removed). The biopsy finding of Acinar adenocarcinoma was consistent with the prostatectomy specimen. The uncertainty in the prognosis is significantly widened by the missing nodal sampling, as pNx does not equate to pN0. Postoperative PSA and its trajectory are critical unknowns that would substantially revise this assessment. Further information regarding postoperative PSA levels and subsequent changes in this metric is necessary to refine the outlook. The fixed estimated horizon is 52.24 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 33.95–70.52 months; its coverage has not been validated.
